sentences.text: Revenue grew from $38.5 billion in FY2016 [F1] to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F10], a 6.4% CAGR [F201], while operating income compounded at 28.6% [F202].
Operating margin rose from 3.0% [F21] to 16.5% [F30], with the largest single step in FY2017, when it rose 6.8pp [D52].
The FY2020 revenue fall of 22.4% [D198] was attributed to lower sales volume from weaker end-user demand and dealer inventory reductions [P59].
The FY2023 operating income jump of 64.0% [D358] was attributed to price realization, higher volume and the absence of a $925 million FY2022 goodwill impairment [X117][P31].
Power Energy contributed 5.2pp [D759] of the 4.3% revenue growth [D463], on a 47.6% revenue share [D757].
Power Generation alone added 3.9pp [D895] of that 5.2pp [D759], on 32.5% growth [D894].
Group growth was attributed to higher sales volume of $3.389 billion, mainly higher sales of equipment to end users [P13]; the filings give no segment cause for Power Energy.
Construction Industries' 1.6% sales decline [D765], which cost 0.6pp of growth [D766], was attributed to unfavorable price realization of $1.136 billion, partly offset by higher volume [P8].
Operating income fell 14.7% [D464] while operating costs grew 9.1% [D481] and revenue 4.3% [D463], giving an incremental margin of -69.1% [D488].
Diluted EPS fell 14.7% [D467], with the diluted share count down 3.5% [D483] offsetting part of the 17.7% net income fall [D465], which is proxy-sourced and within 0.06% of the 10-K [R3].
Operating margin of 16.5% [F30] sits above its 14.3% window median [D1123] and below the 20.2% high [D1122], against an industrials peer median of 15.3% [D1144].
Operating margin fell 3.7pp [D476] as cost of revenue rose to 66.2% of revenue from 62.0% [D441][D388], a 4.2pp drag [D490].
The 4.2pp drag [D490] was attributed to unfavorable manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion, largely from higher tariffs, and unfavorable price realization of $817 million [P9].
The largest window move, FY2017's 6.8pp [D52], came mainly from cost of revenue at 4.0pp [D66], using first-reported R&D and SG&A values [R4][R5].
Net margin of 13.1% [F50] sits 3.4pp below operating margin [F30]; the effective tax rate rose to 24.0% [D449] from 19.7% [D396], a move the cited filings do not explain.
Operating cash flow was 1.32x net income [D450] and free cash flow 1.00x [D451], against a 0.96x window median [D1135], with free cash flow of $8.92 billion [F100].
The 13.2% free cash flow margin [D447] is above its 11.9% median [D1129], but capex grew 41.9% to $2.82 billion [D470][F90] and reached 1.25x D&A [D452].
MP&E operating cash flow rose to $12.3 billion [P4] on lower working-capital requirements and lower cash taxes paid.
Consolidated operating cash flow fell 2.5% [D468] while receivables rose 17.6% [D486] and inventory 7.8% [D487], so the segment release is not visible at group level.

Net cash was -$26.2 billion in FY2025 [D456], wider than -$24.9 billion in FY2024 [D403]; at -38.8% of revenue [D457] it sits near the industrials peer median of -35.6% [D1152], at the 43rd percentile of seven peers [D1151].
Cash of $9.98 billion [F140] and a 1.44x current ratio [F180] are near the 1.40x window median [D1138], while total debt rose 14.1% to $36.2 billion [D485][D455].
Buybacks of $5.19 billion [X140] and dividends of $2.75 billion [X150] absorbed 89.0% of free cash flow [D459], down from 102.9% in FY2024 [D406], and the diluted share count fell 3.5% [D483].
Total debt rose 14.1% [D485], which the filing attributes in part to Financial Products' increased intercompany borrowings from MP&E and external borrowings [P2].
Operating profit fell 14.7% [D464] on a 4.3% revenue gain [D463], attributed to unfavorable manufacturing costs, largely from higher tariffs, and unfavorable price realization [P9].
This matters most because the filing expects higher manufacturing costs to partly offset volume gains in Construction Industries and Power & Energy in Q1 2026 [P14].
R1 is long-running rather than new: net cash has been negative in every year since FY2016 [D14].
Net income for FY2021 to FY2025 is proxy-sourced, within 0.06% of the 10-K [R3], and R2 is dropped because revenue grew 4.3% in FY2025 [D463].
Operating margin back above 16.5% [F30] would confirm the cost drag is easing; a fall below the 14.3% window median [D1123] would reverse the trend, as shown in the FY2026 10-K.
Free cash flow conversion at or above 1.00x [D451] supports the cash base; a fall below the 0.96x window median [D1135] would reverse it, as shown in the FY2026 10-K.
Machine dealer inventory is guided to rise in excess of $1.0 billion in Q1 2026 [P16]; a smaller build would weaken FY2026 volume support, as shown in the Q1 2026 quarterly report.
